questions.question: Train A travelling at 60 km/h takes 20 seconds to cross train B completely, travelling at 48 km/h in the opposite direction. The length of train B is 1.5 times the length of train A. Train B passes a tunnel in 57 seconds. The length (in m) of the tunnel is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Train A = 60 km/h

Speed of Train B = 48 km/h

Crossing time = 20 s

Length of Train B = 1.5 × Length of Train A

Train B passes tunnel in 57 s

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (opposite direction) = speedA + speedB

Speed (m/s) = speed (km/h) ÷ 3.6

Total crossing length = relative speed × time

Tunnel length = total distance while passing tunnel − length of train

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h

⇒ Relative speed = 108 ÷ 3.6 = 30 m/s

⇒ Total crossing length = 30 × 20 = 600

⇒ Let length of Train A = L

⇒ Length of Train B = 1.5L

⇒ L + 1.5L = 600

⇒ 2.5L = 600

⇒ L = 600 ÷ 2.5 = 240

⇒ Length of Train B = 1.5 × 240 = 360

⇒ Speed of Train B = 48 ÷ 3.6 = 13.33 m/s

⇒ Distance covered while passing tunnel = 13.33 × 57 = 760

⇒ Tunnel length = 760 − 360

⇒ Tunnel length = 400

**∴ The correct answer is 400.**

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 10 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled?

Efficiencies: A = 60 ÷ 12 = 5, B = 60 ÷ 15 = 4, C = −(60 ÷ 10) = −6.

Combined efficiency of all three pipes = 5 + 4 − 6 = 3 units/hr.

Time required to fill the tank = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 12 hours

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the tank = 15 hours

Time taken by Pipe C to empty the tank = 10 hours

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

questions.question: What is the major function of a cell wall?

options.text: It works as a storage for material

It is responsible for cell division
It helps in synthesis of carbohydrate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides shape and rigidity to the cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell walls **are a feature of almost all** prokaryotic cells**, as well as many **eukaryotic organisms.**
 
• In addition to providing structural support and maintaining the shape of the cell, The cell wall serves as a **protective barrier** against **physical** and** biological threats.**
 
• It also allows the cell to **withstand** the difference in **osmotic pressure** between the **cell's interior and its environment.**
 
• However, it is not primarily involved in functions such as storage of material, cell division, or the synthesis of carbohydrates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The structure of a typical cell, whether it is a **prokaryotic cell (such as bacteria)** or a **eukaryotic cell (like those found in plants and animals),** includes several key components:

 
• **Cell Membrane (Plasma Membrane):** It controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• **Cytoplasm: **This is the jelly-like substance within the cell membrane, which contains all the organelles.
 
• **Nucleus:** In eukaryotic cells, this organelle contains the cell's DNA and controls the cell's growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• **Mitochondria: ** They generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** There are two types: rough ER, which has ribosomes on its surface, and smooth ER, which lacks ribosomes.
 
• **Golgi Apparatus:** This organelle is involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins for secretion.
 
• **Lysosomes: **They digest excess or worn-out organelles, food particles, and engulfed viruses or bacteria.
 
• **Ribosomes:** They can be found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• **Vacuoles:** These are storage bubbles found in cells. 
 
• **Cell Wall (only in plant cells, fungi, and some protists and bacteria):** It provides and maintains the shape of these cells and serves as a protective barrier.
 
• **Chloroplasts (only in plant cells and some protists):** They are the site of photosynthesis, where light energy is converted into chemical energy.

questions.question: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror at infinity. Which one of the following is correct for its image?

options.text: A real and inverted image would be formed at the focal point.
A virtual and inverted image would be formed at the focal point.
A real and erect image would be formed at infinity.
A virtual and erect image would be formed at the focal point.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A real and inverted image would be formed at the focal point.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a type of spherical mirror where the reflecting surface is curved inward, resembling the interior of a sphere.
 
• When an object is placed at **infinity**, the rays of light coming from the object are parallel to the principal axis of the mirror.
 
• These parallel rays converge at the **focal point** after reflecting off the concave mirror.
 
• The image formed is **real**, meaning it can be projected onto a screen, and it is **inverted** because of the nature of the reflection in concave mirrors.
 
• The position of the image is exactly at the **focus (focal point)** of the mirror, which is located between the center of curvature and the vertex of the mirror.
 
• This property of concave mirrors is widely used in applications such as **telescopes, shaving mirrors, and headlights** of vehicles.
 
• Real and inverted images are a hallmark of concave mirrors when the object is at infinity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A virtual and inverted image would be formed at the focal point**__

 __
 
• A **virtual image** is formed when rays of light appear to meet at a point, but in the case of a concave mirror, an image at the focal point is always **real and inverted** when the object is at infinity.
 
• This statement is incorrect as concave mirrors do not form virtual images at the focal point for objects at infinity.
 
 
 
• **A real and erect image would be formed at infinity**__
 __
 
• Real images formed by concave mirrors are always **inverted**, not erect, unless the object is between the pole and the focus.
 
• This statement is incorrect as the image of an object at infinity is formed at the focal point, not at infinity.
 
 
 
• **A virtual and erect image would be formed at the focal point**__
 
 
• Virtual and erect images are formed only when the object is placed **between the pole and the focus** of the concave mirror.
 
• For an object at infinity, the image formed is real, inverted, and at the focal point, making this statement incorrect.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Lipid synthesis**

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is a membrane-bound organelle present in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Unlike the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER), the SER lacks ribosomes on its surface, giving it a smooth appearance.
 
• The SER plays a crucial role in various metabolic processes, primarily lipid synthesis, detoxification, and calcium storage.
 
• The SER is primarily responsible for the synthesis of lipids, including phospholipids and cholesterol, which are essential components of cellular membranes.
 
• It plays a critical role in the production of steroid hormones, especially in cells of endocrine glands like the adrenal cortex and gonads.
 
• The SER is also involved in the synthesis of triglycerides, which serve as energy storage molecules in adipocytes (fat cells).
 
• In liver cells, the SER contributes to the production of lipoproteins, which transport lipids throughout the body.

**Other Options:**__

 
• **Protein synthesis:** This is the primary role of the Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER), not the SER. The RER is studded with ribosomes, which are responsible for translating mRNA into proteins.
 
• **Photosynthesis:** Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, which are specialized organelles found in plant cells and algae.
 
• **ATP synthesis:** ATP synthesis is primarily the function of mitochondria, known as the powerhouse of the cell. Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction is different from sexual reproduction. Which of the following options does not represent asexual reproduction?

options.text: Involvement of both male and female reproductive organs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involvement of both male and female reproductive organs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** involves a single parent and does not require the participation of both male and female reproductive organs. Hence, the involvement of both male and female reproductive organs__ does not represent asexual reproduction. This is because asexual reproduction does not involve gametes or sexual organs.
 
• **Fission** is a type of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into two or more daughter cells, each of which becomes an independent organism. Examples include amoeba and bacteria. This process does not require male and female reproductive organs.
 
• **Regeneration** is another mode of asexual reproduction where organisms regrow lost or damaged parts, and in some cases, these parts develop into a new organism. For example, planarians and starfish exhibit regeneration. Male and female reproductive organs are not involved in this process.
 
• **Binary fission** is a specific type of fission where an organism divides into two equal parts. This is commonly seen in unicellular organisms like bacteria and protozoa. Again, this process does not involve male and female reproductive organs.
 
• Asexual reproduction is fundamentally different from sexual reproduction, as it does not require the fusion of male and female gametes. Instead, it involves a single organism replicating itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key characteristics of asexual reproduction:**

 
 
• It involves only one parent, and the offspring are genetically identical to the parent.
 
• It occurs in both unicellular and multicellular organisms, such as bacteria, algae, fungi, and certain plants and animals.
 
• Common methods of asexual reproduction include binary fission, budding, fragmentation, regeneration, and vegetative propagation.
 
 
 
• **Types of asexual reproduction:**
 
 
• **Binary fission:** Common in prokaryotic organisms like bacteria. The parent cell splits into two identical daughter cells.
 
• **Budding:** Seen in organisms like yeast and hydra. A new organism grows as a small bud on the parent organism and eventually detaches.
 
• **Fragmentation:** Found in organisms like spirogyra and flatworms. The body of the organism breaks into fragments, each developing into a new organism.
 
• **Vegetative propagation:** Common in plants, where parts like stems, roots, or leaves give rise to new plants. Examples include potato tubers and bryophyllum leaves.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with sexual reproduction:**
 
 
• Sexual reproduction requires the involvement of two parents, with male and female gametes fusing to form a zygote.
 
• Offspring produced sexually show genetic variation, unlike asexual reproduction where offspring are clones of the parent.
 
• Sexual reproduction involves complex reproductive organs and processes, whereas asexual reproduction is simpler and faster.
 
 
 
• **Examples of organisms showing asexual reproduction:**
 
 
• **Binary fission:** Amoeba, Paramecium, and Euglena.
 
• **Budding:** Hydra and yeast.
 
• **Regeneration:** Starfish and planarians.
 
• **Vegetative propagation:** Potato, ginger, and onion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of asexual reproduction:**

 
 
• It is a quick and efficient mode of reproduction, especially in stable environments.
 
• It does not require a mate, which is advantageous in isolated conditions.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of asexual reproduction:**
 
 
• Lack of genetic variation can make organisms vulnerable to environmental changes.
 
• It may lead to the accumulation of harmful mutations over generations.

• **The liver** is also involved in metabolizing fats, proteins, and carbohydrates, ensuring the body receives adequate energy and nutrients.
 
• It is responsible for breaking down toxins such as alcohol and drugs, and removing harmful substances from the bloodstream. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*

• **Xylem** is a vascular tissue in plants responsible for the transport of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• Xylem consists of specialized cells such as **tracheids** and **vessel elements**, which are tubular and help in the upward movement of water through capillary action.
 
• The transport in xylem is a passive process driven by physical forces like **transpiration pull**, cohesion, and adhesion of water molecules.

• Unlike xylem, phloem transport is bidirectional, meaning nutrients can move both upward and downward in the plant.

questions.question: The aqueous solution of copper sulphate is:
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

The nature of an aqueous solution of copper sulfate (CuSO₄) is determined by the hydrolysis of its constituent ions.

__
 
• Copper sulfate dissociates in water as:
 
CuSO₄ → Cu²⁺ + SO₄²⁻

 
 
• The Cu²⁺ ion (a transition metal ion) undergoes hydrolysis in water to form a weakly acidic solution. This occurs because Cu²⁺ has a high charge density and attracts water molecules, forming a hydrated complex.
 
• In the hydrated complex, water molecules act as ligands. One of the water molecules donates a proton (H⁺) to the solution, causing acidity:
 
[Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ → [Cu(H₂O)₅(OH)]⁺ + H⁺

 
 
• The release of H⁺ ions makes the solution acidic.

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• When copper sulfate dissolves in water, the Cu²⁺ ion is the primary contributor to the acidity of the solution due to hydrolysis.
 
• SO₄²⁻ (sulfate ion) does not undergo hydrolysis, as it is the conjugate base of a strong acid (H₂SO₄) and remains inert in water.
 
• As a result, the solution becomes acidic due to the hydrolysis of Cu²⁺.

**Therefore, the aqueous solution of copper sulfate is acidic.**

questions.question:
With reference to India’s Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) programme, consider the following statements:

I. SSLV is designed with a modular architecture allowing integration and launch readiness in less than 72 hours.

II. Unlike PSLV and GSLV, SSLV is entirely road-transportable, enabling launch from multiple terrestrial and mobile platforms.

III. The 100th technology transfer agreement signed in 2025 aims to make HAL the sole global commercial provider of SSLVs without ISRO’s future involvement.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• ISRO, NSIL, IN-SPACe, and HAL signed the 100th technology transfer agreement, enabling HAL to independently produce SSLVs over 24 months with ISRO’s guidance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• SSLV is designed with **modular assembly and minimal infrastructure requirements**, allowing integration and launch readiness within **~72 hours** (much faster than PSLV/GSLV). **Hence, Statement 1 is correct.**
 
• SSLV is road-transportable and compact, enabling potential launches from multiple terrestrial launch pads. This is a key feature for flexibility in launching from Sriharikota and Kulasekarapattinam. **Hence, Statement II is correct**.
 
• The technology transfer to HAL does **not eliminate ISRO’s involvement**. ISRO continues to provide training, technical support, and mission-readiness guidance. HAL is not the *sole* global provider; NSIL manages commercialization and foreign launches. **Hence, Statement III is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with PSLV/GSLV:
 
 
• PSLV & GSLV require complex infrastructure and longer integration (~weeks).
 
• SSLV is simplified, cost-efficient, and quicker, tailored for small satellites.
 
 
 
• Strategic importance:
 
 
• Expected to capture demand from the $7-8 billion global small-satellite launch market.
 
• Will enhance India’s competitiveness against Rocket Lab’s Electron and SpaceX’s rideshare programmes.
 
 
 
• Policy significance:
 
 
• Facilitated under space-sector reforms (IN-SPACe, NSIL) to integrate private industry in end-to-end launch vehicle production.

questions.question: The "Basic Structure Doctrine," which limits Parliament's amending powers to prevent changes to the Constitution's essential features, was established in which landmark Supreme Court case?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesavananda Bharati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)** case is considered a landmark judgment by the Supreme Court of India.
 
• This case established the **"Basic Structure Doctrine"**, which limits Parliament's power to amend the Constitution in a way that alters its essential features.
 
• The judgment clarified that while Parliament has wide powers to amend the Constitution under Article 368, it cannot destroy or tamper with the fundamental framework or basic structure of the Constitution.
 
• The basic structure includes principles such as **separation of powers, fundamental rights, secularism, democracy**, and other essential elements.
 
• The ruling was delivered by a 13-judge bench, the largest bench ever constituted in the history of the Indian judiciary, and was decided by a thin majority of 7:6.
 
• This doctrine has since been pivotal in safeguarding constitutional integrity and protecting democratic values in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980):**

 
 
• This case reinforced the Basic Structure Doctrine established in Kesavananda Bharati.
 
• The court struck down certain amendments to the Constitution, ruling that they violated the basic structure by curtailing judicial review powers.
 
• It emphasized the balance between fundamental rights and directive principles, stating that neither could override the other.
 
• The judgment further strengthened the doctrine by ensuring judicial scrutiny of constitutional amendments.
 
 
 
• **Indira Sawhney v. Union of India (1992):**
 
 
• Also known as the Mandal Commission case, it dealt with reservations for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in government jobs and educational institutions.
 
• The Supreme Court upheld the 27% reservation for OBCs but introduced the concept of the "creamy layer," excluding economically advanced individuals within OBCs.
 
• This case focused on social justice and equality but did not involve the Basic Structure Doctrine.
 
 
 
• **A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950):**
 
 
• This case dealt with preventive detention laws and the interpretation of Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty).
 
• The Supreme Court ruled that the procedure established by law is sufficient to restrict personal liberty, limiting the scope of Article 21.
 
• However, this case was later overruled in **Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)**, which expanded the interpretation of Article 21.
 
• This case did not address the Basic Structure Doctrine.
 
 
 
• **Basic Structure Doctrine:**
 
 
• The doctrine ensures that certain fundamental aspects of the Constitution, such as sovereignty, secularism, democracy, judicial independence, and fundamental rights, remain unaltered.
 
• It acts as a safeguard against arbitrary amendments that could undermine constitutional principles.
 
• The doctrine has been applied in multiple cases, including **Minerva Mills, Waman Rao, and S.R. Bommai**, to protect the Constitution's integrity.

questions.question: The concept of 'Retreating monsoon' in India is related to which of the following?

options.text: Southward retreat of monsoon winds from the Indian subcontinent
Gradual decrease in temperature during the winter months
Formation of cyclonic storms in the Bay of Bengal
Pre-monsoon rains arrive in southern states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Southward retreat of monsoon winds from the Indian subcontinent.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Retreating Monsoon:** This term refers to the **southward withdrawal of monsoon winds** from the Indian subcontinent. The monsoon begins to retreat from the northern regions in early September and withdraws completely by November.
 
• During this process, the winds reverse direction from the southwest to the northeast, bringing dry weather to most parts of the country. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Gradual decrease in temperature:** The retreating monsoon coincides with the onset of autumn and winter in India. As the winds withdraw, temperatures begin to drop, particularly in northern and central India. *Statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Formation of cyclonic storms:** The retreating monsoon leads to the formation of cyclonic storms in the **Bay of Bengal**. These storms often affect eastern and southern coastal regions, bringing heavy rainfall and causing destruction. *Statement 3 is correct.*
 
• **Pre-monsoon rains:** The retreating monsoon is associated with post-monsoon rains, particularly in southern India. This includes the **Northeast Monsoon**, which brings rainfall to Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka. *Statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Southward retreat of monsoon winds from the Indian subcontinent.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Retreating Monsoon:**

 
 
• **Duration:** The retreating monsoon begins in **September** and ends in **November**.
 
• **Direction:** Winds reverse from southwest to northeast, marking the withdrawal of monsoon winds.
 
• **Dry Weather:** Most parts of India experience **dry conditions** during this phase, particularly in northern and western regions.
 
• **Rainfall:** Southern India, especially Tamil Nadu, receives rainfall due to the **Northeast Monsoon**.
 
 
 
• **Cyclonic Activity:**
 
 
• Cyclonic storms are common in the **Bay of Bengal** during this period. These storms frequently impact coastal states such as Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal.
 
• **Example:** Cyclone Phailin (2013) and Cyclone Hudhud (2014) occurred during the retreating monsoon.
 
 
 
• **Northeast Monsoon:**
 
 
• It brings rainfall to Tamil Nadu, southern Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka. This monsoon is essential for agricultural activities in these regions.
 
• **Example:** Tamil Nadu receives about **50%-60%** of its annual rainfall from the Northeast Monsoon.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Factors Influencing Retreating Monsoon:**

 
 
• **Pressure Systems:** The withdrawal is influenced by the development of **high-pressure systems** over northern India.
 
• **Temperature Gradient:** A decrease in temperature leads to changes in wind direction.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• The retreating monsoon affects agricultural activities, particularly the harvesting of summer crops.
 
• It also has a significant impact on regions prone to cyclonic storms, causing damage to infrastructure and livelihoods.

questions.question: When is National Engineer's Day observed?

__
 
• National Engineer's Day is observed every year on **15 September** in India.
 
• The day commemorates the birth anniversary of **Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya**, a renowned engineer and Bharat Ratna awardee.
 
• Sir M. Visvesvaraya is known for his outstanding contributions in the field of engineering and his role in the construction of dams, irrigation systems, and flood control mechanisms in India.
 
• The day serves to recognize the contributions of engineers in nation-building and to inspire young minds to pursue careers in engineering and technology.
 
• National Engineer's Day is celebrated with events such as technical seminars, workshops, and discussions in engineering institutions across the country.

• This day is observed as **Human Rights Day** globally, commemorating the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948.
 
• The day highlights the importance of human rights and promotes equality, justice, and human dignity.
 
 
 
• **14 April:**
 
 
• 14 April is celebrated as **Ambedkar Jayanti**, marking the birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The day is also observed to promote social justice and equality, as Dr. Ambedkar was a staunch advocate of marginalized communities' rights.
 
 
 
• **1 October:**
 
 
• 1 October is globally observed as **International Day of Older Persons**, as designated by the United Nations in 1990.
 
• The day aims to raise awareness about issues affecting older adults, such as elder abuse and healthcare, and to appreciate their contributions to society.
